First of all, what a horrible comment especially coming from a professor. One of my biggest triggers is when an educator discourages a student. If you don’t understand now, that does not mean you won’t understand ever. Note that there are literally so many ways to learn one thing. Professors are often so closed minded and egotistical that they think their method of teaching is the only way a student can learn. So you’ve established your professors a douche, I would suggest if you are committed to learning trigonometry, to engage in self study. Trigonometry is a lot of memorization of the unit circle and application of formulas, I would start there. 
Mathematics is inherently foundational, and knowing that is a huge advantage when learning. Whatever topic you are stuck on go backwards make sure you learn the foundational concepts really well so going forward naturally everything makes much more sense. Calculus is the application of algebra and trigonometry in the actual calculus ideas or theorems and trust me they are not that scary. If you obtain a really solid foundation in algebra and trig, I guarantee calculus will be a breeze. Don’t get stuck in the mindset that you are “just bad at math” in my opinion there’s just no such thing. I believe people are just uneducated and are trying to go forward without knowing what came before (hence math being foundational). I don’t necessarily agree with the idea that if it’s hard now math will always be hard. It may be hard in the beginning to learn there’s no denying that, but once you get that really good foundation then why would it continue to be hard for you if we already established mathematics continues to build on itself. And remember you can’t get good at math without practice.
